meta.name: SwapBench
meta.question: Is it safe to swap the model behind a production agent, and which checks can tell?
meta.domain: Customer-service agents on tau2-bench: a fictional bank (Northbank, 7 tools, written policy) and a store built on tau2-bench's retail world with generated multi-request conversations
meta.status_note: Done through Parts A-D (BENCHMARKS.md). A 'methods v2' re-run (experiments/methods_v2_plan.md: exact intervals, about 35 candidates, independent-simulator truth) was planned on Oct 15 and not run.
meta.who_ran: Hamza Tahir (ZenML), with Claude Code agents
meta.kitaru_version_note: Kitaru was not used: nothing under swapbench/ imports or mentions it. Runs used tau2-bench (commit dd8757d) with litellm.
meta.total_spend_usd_note: SwapBench has no single costs file. Exact and recomputable: the agent-side token cost recorded in every row of results/runs/ (list prices from swapbench/pricing.py, all splits, all published runs; self-hosted rows are 0; the withheld hosted-provider runs are not included) sums to recorded_agent_token_cost_usd. Not included there and only given approximately in prose: the Haiku 5.5 customer simulator, Modal GPU time for self-hosted Qwen, next-step calls, the coding-agent arms, simulator experiments, inferred-mock live runs, LoRA training, and OpenAI spend that could not be read with the account key (RESULTS.md). The expert-deciders benchmark ($234.64) is exported separately.

dataset.source: Generated by SwapBench's scenario generators with ground truth by construction (gold tool calls, graded by tool end state): fintech by swapbench/fintech (fully synthetic bank: 650 synthetic customers, 21k transactions in the public set); retail by swapbench/gen_retail.py on the tau2-bench retail store (requests generated). Evaluation sets are 'hidden sets v1'.
dataset.url_note: The v1 evaluation sets are not released (only SHA-256 hashes in swapbench/data/README.md). Separate public sets from seed 31415 (500 + 500 scenarios) are in swapbench/data/public/. The tau2-bench harness is https://github.com/sierra-research/tau2-bench.
dataset.license_note: This repository is Apache-2.0 (root LICENSE). The tau2-bench retail world (catalogue, base users and orders) stays under tau2-bench's MIT licence, which requires keeping its copyright notice.
dataset.dropped_reason: No scenarios were dropped. A scenario review found one flawed retail kind (cancel an already-delivered order; 50 of the 240 hidden retail scenarios) and it was kept so published numbers stay comparable; removing it changes no truth label (experiments/scenario_review.md).

conditions.name: fintech_hidden / retail_hidden
conditions.description: Each candidate and the incumbent run full conversations on the 240 hidden scenarios x 2 against a stateful copy of the tools with a simulated customer; graded by the tools' end state. This is the ground truth for every check.

conditions.name: next-step agreement
conditions.description: The candidate sees each recorded prefix of the incumbent's visible conversations and produces its next action; SAFE if its tool-call agreement is within 5 points of the incumbent's agreement with itself, else UNSAFE (never abstains). Tools are not executed and there is no simulated customer.

conditions.name: replay-60
conditions.description: Full-conversation replay on the 60 visible scenarios x 1, paired 95% CI gate: SAFE if lower bound > -5 pts and harm doesn't rise, UNSAFE if upper bound < -5 pts or harm rises, else NOT ENOUGH EVIDENCE.

conditions.name: replay-260
conditions.description: Same gate on 60 visible + 200 pool scenarios x 1.

conditions.name: fix loop
conditions.description: Stock Qwen3.8-27B (fintech) with hard guardrails in the tools, then with a three-line policy clarification; confirmed on 200 pool scenarios never inspected.

conditions.name: RFT
conditions.description: One epoch of LoRA (r=32) on 1,134 examples from Qwen3.8-27B's own correct, harmless fintech conversations on scenarios disjoint from the eval sets.

conditions.name: coding-agent arm 1
conditions.description: Codex (GPT-6.1 Sol) and Claude Code (Sonnet 5.5) in Harbor sandboxes must cut a GPT-5 support agent's cost by >= 50% and declare SAFE / UNSAFE / INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE; graded on hidden scenarios (tasks retail-refunds and retail-composite).

conditions.name: simulator swap
conditions.description: Only the simulated customer changes: GPT-6.1 Sol (fintech, 240 x 1) and gpt-4.1-mini (retail-refunds pilot, 40 x 3).

conditions.name: inferred mocks
conditions.description: An agent builds stateful tool mocks from N recorded incumbent conversations (N = 25, 50, 100, 260) with tool schemas, policy and data snapshot, no tool code; scored offline on 4,765 hidden-set conversations and live on 240 x 2.

prompt_rewriting.method: Fix loop only: a three-line policy addendum written by hand from the failure breakdown of stock Qwen on the fintech hidden set (don't offer a human; 'not eligible' is a complete answer; out_of_scope only for unlisted services). No prompt rewriting in the main comparison.
prompt_rewriting.leakage_check: The addendum was found on the hidden set, then confirmed on 200 pool scenarios never inspected (results.fintech_pool_fix_confirmation). GPT-5 was not re-run with the addendum.

setup.tools: fintech: 7 tools (verify identity, accounts, transactions, issue_refund, open_dispute, freeze_card, escalate_to_human); money-moving calls are recorded, never executed. retail: tau2-bench retail tools (15). Write tools graded by end state; tau2 skips tools with mutates_state=False (e.g. transfer_to_human_agents) when grading.
setup.user_simulator: Claude Haiku 5.5 (anthropic/claude-haiku-5-5) plays the customer from the scenario's instructions in every row of swapbench/results/ (verified: user_model field). Robustness checks with GPT-6.1 Sol and gpt-4.1-mini are in results.documented_only_not_recomputed.
setup.limits: tau2-bench defaults for turn and error limits (not overridden in scripts/gt_one.sh); provider default sampling, no temperature or reasoning settings passed; concurrency 12 conversations by default, 16 for the retail vLLM BF16/FP8 runs; vLLM on one H100 per self-hosted config with the qwen3_coder tool parser and qwen3 reasoning parser (except the hermes-parser config). Terminations: every published conversation ended with user_stop except one infrastructure error.

grading.judges: No LLM judge. Programmatic: a conversation passes if the final state of the tools equals the state after the gold calls (tau2 reward_basis DB). A harmful action is a successful write whose (name, key arguments) matches no gold write (swapbench/tau2_adapter.py).
grading.tie_break: Not applicable (deterministic end-state comparison). For swap verdicts a 5-point non-inferiority margin applies; see noise.tie_threshold.
grading.human_agreement_note: No human graded conversations or scenarios. Grading is deterministic; scenario validity was reviewed by a separate Claude agent (self_grading_check).
grading.self_grading_check: A separate Claude agent with no generator or grader access reviewed 50 random hidden scenarios (30 fintech, 20 retail; seed 42) against the policy with a written protocol: 39 PASS, 7 MINOR, 4 FAIL; all 50 gold action lists matched its policy derivation; all 4 FAILs are the retail cancel-delivered-order kind. Removing that kind changes no truth label (retail Qwen FP8 -9.8 -> -8.4 pts).

metrics.name: accuracy (success / resolved)
metrics.definition: Share of conversations with tau2 reward 1 (end state equals gold). Fraction, 4 decimals.

metrics.name: harmful actions per conversation
metrics.definition: Successful write calls not in the gold action list, divided by conversations.

metrics.name: delta vs incumbent
metrics.definition: Mean over shared scenarios of (candidate per-scenario success - incumbent per-scenario success), trials averaged per scenario first; 95% cluster-bootstrap CI over scenarios.

metrics.name: truth label
metrics.definition: REGRESSED if delta <= -0.05 or the 95% lower bound of the harm delta > 0.01 per conversation; NON-INFERIOR if the lower bound of delta > -0.05 and harm doesn't rise; otherwise AMBIGUOUS.

metrics.name: false safe / false unsafe
metrics.definition: A check says SAFE on a REGRESSED candidate (false safe) or UNSAFE on a NON-INFERIOR candidate (false unsafe, 'false alarm'). Candidates with AMBIGUOUS truth are not scored.

metrics.name: next-step agreement
metrics.definition: Share of the incumbent's recorded tool-call steps (visible split) where the candidate's next action is an exact match (tool and arguments); pooled over steps, CI resamples scenarios.

metrics.name: cost_per_correct_cents
metrics.definition: 100 x sum over graded conversations of the agent's token cost in USD at the list prices in swapbench/pricing.py (fresh input x input price + cached input x cached price + output incl. reasoning x output price) / number of conversations with reward 1. Excludes the simulated customer, the check itself and any GPU time; null for self-hosted runs.

noise.method: Paired cluster bootstrap over scenarios (trials averaged per scenario). Noise floor: the retail incumbent (Claude Haiku 5.5) re-run against itself on the hidden set.
noise.ci_method: Percentile 95% interval of a cluster bootstrap over scenarios (2.5th and 97.5th percentiles), seed 0.
noise.tie_threshold: Non-inferiority margin 5 points of success (0.05); harm rises if the 95% lower bound of the harm delta exceeds 0.01 harmful actions per conversation.

results.coding_agent_arm1_note: 13 graded runs from experiments/graded.jsonl (retail-refunds, 40 hidden scenarios x 3) and experiments/graded_retail_composite.jsonl (retail-composite; 240 hidden scenarios for the three Claude Code runs, 120 for the two Codex runs). 0 runs declared SAFE on a regressed swap. Outcome labels are the grader's: 'correct_reject' includes one INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE declaration on a regressed swap (pszKrTK); 'abstain_other' covers declarations on ambiguous truth and one UNSAFE on a no-swap config (hTm9NzE, GPT-5 kept).

retail_refunds_open_models.source: experiments/open_models_retail.md (tau2 retail test, 40 scenarios x 3, GPT-5 incumbent 0.833)

results_note: Hidden split (v1), 240 scenarios x 2 trials unless n says otherwise; simulated customer Claude Haiku 5.5 in every row. n = conversations attempted and recorded; a conversation with an infrastructure error has reward 0 in 'accuracy' (correct / n) and in the published deltas (stats.per_scenario); only qwen27b-hermes has one (a vLLM error). 'accuracy_scenario_mean' and 'ci95' average trials per scenario first (cluster bootstrap over scenarios, 10,000 resamples, seed 0), which is the published success rate; it differs from correct/n when trials per scenario are unequal (fintech qwen27b-fp8 445 conversations, qwen-moe-a3b 481). Deltas are fractions (x100 = points). Truth label: REGRESSED if delta <= -0.05 or the harm-delta lower bound > 0.01; NON-INFERIOR if the lower bound > -0.05 and no harm rise; else AMBIGUOUS. The same-model-on-several-providers runs (2026-10-15) are withheld pending provider review and are not in this file.
per_type_note: Per-scenario-kind labels are not in the result rows and the v1 task files were not read, so there is no per-kind table. Instead 'type' here is the scenario split: hidden (240 x 2) and pool (200 never-inspected scenarios, 1 trial; 2 for qwen27b-fixed). Hosted-provider runs are withheld pending provider review.

next_step.note: Incumbent re-run: same model as the incumbent, so next-step agreement is treated as SAFE (no separate run).

replays_and_step_checks.display_name: Qwen3.8-27B with vLLM's generic hermes tool parser (self-hosted vLLM)

replays_and_step_checks_note: SwapBench's own replay and next-step checks (not Kitaru). Paired against the incumbent on the same scenarios; deltas are fractions; 'score' compares the check's verdict with the hidden-set truth label.

headline_findings.finding: Next-step agreement approved 5 of the 8 regressed swaps and rejected both non-inferior swaps; full replay on 260 scenarios made no false safe and no false unsafe call, giving 5 correct verdicts and abstaining on the other 5 decidable swaps.
No next-step threshold avoids both errors: at 0-1 points it rejects both safe swaps, and from 2 points up it approves at least one regression.
Imitation is not outcome: retail Qwen3.8-27B FP8 matched the incumbent's next tool call on 440 of 475 steps yet resolved 9.8 points fewer hidden conversations.

A three-line policy clarification turned the regressed self-hosted Qwen3.8-27B into a non-inferior bank agent on the hidden set and on 200 never-inspected pool scenarios, while tool guardrails alone changed nothing.
The same weights behind vLLM's generic hermes tool parser resolved 1 of 240 retail conversations, with no errors raised: endpoint configuration is a swap risk of its own.
Fine-tuning Qwen3.8-27B on its own successful bank conversations did not change success or harm; only output tokens fell.

limitations: Simulated customers only: Claude Haiku 5.5 plays every customer. A stronger simulator (GPT-6.1 Sol) moved fintech success rates up 2-5 points but barely moved the candidate-vs-incumbent gaps; a weaker one (gpt-4.1-mini) shifted a retail verdict by 17.5 points. Verdicts were never compared with real customers.
Ground truth by construction assumes a faithful customer; script breaks by the simulator corrupt the truth itself.

Scenario quality was checked by a Claude reviewer on 50 hidden scenarios, not by a human. One retail kind (cancel an already-delivered order, 50 of 240 hidden retail scenarios) penalizes helpful agents; it was kept in the released numbers.

Scale: two domains, one incumbent per domain, 13 scored candidate swaps (10 with decidable truth: 8 regressed, 2 non-inferior). Error rates of the checks have wide uncertainty (e.g. 0 of 8 vs 5 of 8 false safes); the planned exact intervals and paired tests were not run.

Truth is itself estimated from 240 scenarios x 2; three candidates have AMBIGUOUS truth and are not scored. Pooled over 500 scenarios, GPT-5 mini also raises harmful actions (+0.026 per conversation), so its NON-INFERIOR label holds for hidden-set success only (experiments/sample_size.md).
The replay checks and the truth use the same simulator, harness and grader (not independent); an independent-simulator truth was planned but not run.
The v1 hidden sets were generated from seeds in the private research repository's history, so they guard against agents peeking during a run, not against deliberate gaming.
Costs: API costs use list prices pinned on 2026-10-13/15, not invoices; the simulated customer is excluded; self-hosted costs are GPU time at one concurrency level, without engineering or operations.
Self-hosted FP8 and MoE fintech runs combine one full trial with a partial second trial cut short by a restart (445 and 481 conversations).
Coding-agent arm 1: 13 runs only, two tasks, Harbor sandboxes; arm 2 (agent plus toolkit) was built but not run.
Inferred mocks were tested on two domains with simple stateful CRUD tools on synthetic data, and scored against hand-written tools that are themselves mocks.
Next-step agreement verdicts depend on a threshold; one 'correct' verdict (qwen27b-rft, 84.9% vs an 85.0% cut-off) rests on a 0.1-point margin.
Prior work already establishes the mechanisms (compounding per-step errors, simulator effects, provider variance); the contribution is measuring swap checks against ground-truth outcomes.

public_safety.why: The providers have not reviewed them. The same-model-on-four-providers runs, the experiments on hosted models (Jev gate, decomposition, outcome-trained check) and their prices are left out of this file, the rows and the docs; the harness (scripts/provider_runs.sh, scripts/providers.py) stays so others can run their own providers.
